source: Kuali Archive Enhancements and Requirements, Security Requirements tab
enforcementState: Record-level access is switched OFF on the development website. Every signed-in user can still reach the whole archive, so none of these requirements can be verified yet.

requirements.requirement: Central users shall have unrestricted access to all system objects and functionality provided by the system.
requirements.audience: PAFO and OSP Administrators, and the Subaward, Contracting, Industry, Foundation Relations and Research Development teams.
requirements.acceptance: Verify a Central User can access all system objects and functionality.
requirements.decisions: Who administers access grants, and whether granting Central access needs a second approver.
requirements.conflict: Five of the seven listed Central teams are not Kuali user roles, so Central membership cannot be derived from record contacts and has to be assigned and maintained by hand. “All system objects” also has to be read against an implementation that starts with Award and adds other record types in later stages.
requirements.recommendation: Central membership should require an explicit, auditable grant rather than being inferred. Five of the seven listed Central teams have no reliable Kuali role to map from, so membership for those cannot be derived from record contacts at all. Module coverage gaps should be shown, so “all system objects” is never read as wider than what is actually built.

requirements.requirement: Department users shall have access to all system objects associated with their assigned department(s).
requirements.acceptance: Verify a Department User can access all objects within their assigned department and cannot access objects from unassigned departments.
requirements.decisions: Whether “department” means the record's lead unit, and whether a unit's sub-units are included. Recorded direction is lead unit, honouring each grant's include-sub-units setting; a unit that led any version of an Award would then see that whole Award.
requirements.conflict: The source document's own role table places PAFO Administrators in Central Users, but names a PAFO Administrator as the Department User test fixture. Which group that person belongs to has to be settled before this requirement can be tested, because the two readings give opposite expected results.
requirements.recommendation: A department-only test identity is needed before this can be proven. A Central or PAFO user cannot demonstrate a department restriction, because unrestricted access would satisfy the test for the wrong reason.

requirements.requirement: Research staff shall have access only to system objects on which they are directly listed as a contact.
requirements.accessScope: Objects directly assigned to the user
requirements.audience: PD/PI Contact, PD/PI Multiple and Co-Investigator.
requirements.acceptance: Verify Research Staff can access assigned objects and cannot access unassigned objects.
requirements.decisions: How a sign-in is tied to a Kuali person, and whether Key Persons count as research staff. Recorded direction is PI, multiple-PI and Co-Investigator, with Key Persons excluded.

requirements.requirement: Other authorized users shall have access only to specifically authorized system objects identified by IO number.
requirements.audience: Users authorised for named records only, typically to help a department with one task.
requirements.acceptance: Verify an Authorized Viewer can access only the specifically authorized IO number(s).
requirements.decisions: Which field is the authoritative IO number, and whether Subaward account numbers count as IO numbers. Recorded direction is the Award account number; Subaward is unresolved.

requirements.requirement: The system shall support adding a user's access at both the role level and the specific IO number level based on the user's authorized role, department assignment, object assignment, or specific IO authorization.
requirements.audience: Whoever administers access for the archive.
requirements.acceptance: Verify an Administrator can add access by assigning a role and/or specific IO number(s).
requirements.decisions: Who holds the administrator role once Kuali is retired, and whether a second approver is required.

requirements.requirement: The system shall support removing a user's access at both the role level and the specific IO number level when the user's role, department assignment, object assignment, or authorization changes.
requirements.audience: Whoever administers access for the archive.
requirements.acceptance: Verify an Administrator can remove a role and/or specific IO access and that access is revoked.
requirements.decisions: Who owns department assignments after retirement, where changes are fed from, and how quickly access must be withdrawn when someone leaves.
requirements.conflict: Being told that someone has left is not the same as their access being withdrawn, and a periodic review is not a withdrawal. Removal has to be an action taken in the archive, within an agreed time, or this requirement is only partly met.
requirements.recommendation: Receiving an offboarding notification is not the same as revoking access in the archive, and should be tracked as two separate events. Behaviour for a session that is already signed in should be documented and tested explicitly. The required revocation interval is left pending rather than assumed.

requirements.requirement: The system shall enforce access restrictions when a user attempts to access a system object for which they are not authorized.
requirements.acceptance: Attempt to access an unauthorized object and verify that access is denied
requirements.decisions: Whether a record outside your access answers “not found” or “not allowed”, and whether hidden related records are counted anywhere a user can see.

recommendationStatus: Recommended, not approved. These are proposals recorded for review; none has been accepted as policy, and none changes how the archive behaves today.
